@pytest.mark.filterwarnings('ignore:default contamination')
@pytest.mark.filterwarnings('ignore:behaviour="old"')
def test_iforest_warm_start():
    """Test that the warm_start parameter adds estimators."""
    X = [[1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 1], [0.3, 4.2], [1.2, 0.4], [0.7, 1.8]]

    # Test that we can fit more than one tree with warm_start=True
    clf = IsolationForest(max_samples=10, random_state=rng,
                          warm_start=True, n_estimators=3)
    clf.fit(X)
    assert len(clf.estimators_) == 3

    clf.set_params(n_estimators=4).fit(X)
    assert len(clf.estimators_) == 4

    # Test that warm_start=False fits a whole new forest
    clf.set_params(warm_start=False, n_estimators=6).fit(X)
    assert len(clf.estimators_) == 6

def test_behaviour_param():
    X_train = [[1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 1]]
    clf1 = IsolationForest(behaviour='old').fit(X_train)
    clf2 = IsolationForest(behaviour='new', contamination='auto').fit(X_train)
    assert_array_equal(clf1.decision_function([[2., 2.]]),

``warm_start`` parameter. When ``warm_start=True``, the estimator reuses the
solution of the previous call to ``fit`` and adds more estimators to the
ensemble (increment ``n_estimators`` accordingly), instead of fitting a whole
new forest from scratch.
